title: Check yourself: data hiding and protection

questions.stem: The constructor `OrderListener(Bus bus, String topic)` runs `bus.subscribe(this)` as its first statement, then throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `topic` is blank, and only after that assigns `this.topic = topic`. A caller passes `"  "`, catches the exception and logs it. The bus delivers each event by calling `listener.topic().startsWith(...)` on every subscriber. What happens at the next event?

options.text: The bus skips the refused listener, since an exception thrown by a constructor removes `this` from wherever the constructor stored it
options.says: the exception only keeps `new` from returning a reference; a reference the constructor already handed out survives

options.text: The bus calls a listener whose topic is `null`, since the bus kept a reference the exception didn't take back
options.says: the listener was subscribed before the check threw, and its field was never assigned, so it holds its default

options.text: The bus skips the refused listener, since an object exists only once its constructor has returned
options.says: the object exists before the constructor body runs; `this` can be handed out from its first line

options.text: The bus calls a listener whose topic is blank, since the constructor's arguments are stored before its body runs
options.says: fields are assigned only by the body's statements, and the throw came before the assignment, so the field is still `null`

origin.section: A Constructor That Fails Has Already Published this If It Registered Itself First

questions.stem: A `Quote` keeps the `BigDecimal` rate passed to its constructor in a `private final` field, without copying it, and has no setters. A partner library passes an instance of its own `TrackedRate extends BigDecimal`. Can what the Quote's rate reports change after the Quote is built?

options.text: No, since a subclass of `BigDecimal` inherits the immutability of the class it extends
options.says: `BigDecimal` isn't final, so a subclass can override its methods and keep state of its own that changes

options.text: Yes, but only through reflection, since the subclass object can't reach the Quote's private field
options.says: nothing needs to write the field: it holds the library's object, which changes on its own

options.text: Yes, since the subclass can override `BigDecimal`'s methods and keep state of its own that changes
options.says: an immutable type must be final (or have only private constructors); `BigDecimal` and `BigInteger` aren't, so a kept instance may be a mutable subclass

options.text: No, since a `final` field with no setter fixes the state of the subclass object it refers to
options.says: a final field fixes the reference, not the referenced object; immutability goes only as deep as the copy

origin.section: An Immutable Class Is final, and Copies Every Mutable Part, Not Just the Collection

questions.stem: A discount must be between 1 and 90 percent. `final class Coupon implements Serializable` checks this in its constructor; `record CouponRecord(int percent) implements Serializable` checks it in its compact constructor. Neither declares `readObject`. A stream of each is edited so the percentage reads 150, then passed to `ObjectInputStream.readObject()`. What comes back?

options.text: Both are refused, since deserialization calls each type's constructor and its check
options.says: for a Serializable class only the no-arg constructor of the first non-serializable superclass runs; the class's own check never does

options.text: Both come back holding 150, since deserialization sets the fields without calling either constructor
options.says: a record is rebuilt through its canonical constructor, so its check runs and the stream is refused

options.text: The record is refused and the class comes back holding 150, since only the record is rebuilt through a constructor
options.says: the record's canonical constructor throws, which readObject() reports as InvalidObjectException; the class's fields are set from the stream

options.text: The class is refused and the record comes back holding 150, since only the class's constructor is called by `readObject()`
options.says: it is the other way round: the class's constructor doesn't run, the record's canonical constructor does

origin.section: Deserialization Builds the Object Without Your Constructor, So readObject Checks Again

questions.stem: A test helper sets fields with `getDeclaredField(name)`, `setAccessible(true)` and `setInt(target, value)`. It sets `row` on `final class Seat { private final int row; ... }`. The team then turns `Seat` into `record Seat(int row)`, and the helper runs again. What does the helper's write do?

options.text: It works before and after the change, since `setAccessible(true)` lifts both `private` and `final`
options.says: Field.set refuses a final field of a record even after setAccessible(true)

options.text: It works on the class and throws `IllegalAccessException` on the record, since `Field.set` refuses a record's final fields
options.says: setAccessible(true) lets reflection write a non-static final field of an ordinary class, not of a record or a hidden class

options.text: It fails before and after the change, since `Field.set` can't write a `final` field once the constructor has returned
options.says: reflection wrote the class's private final field after construction

options.text: It throws `IllegalAccessException` on the class and works on the record, since `Field.set` writes a record's fields through its canonical constructor
options.says: it is the other way round: the class's final field is writable by reflection, the record's isn't

origin.section: Reflection Can Rewrite a private final Field of a Class, but Not of a Record
